dictionary.name: page_id
dictionary.label: Page id
dictionary.definition: Unique key for the page-capture. Format {bank}_{product_family}_{language}_{nn}.

dictionary.name: bank
dictionary.label: Bank
dictionary.definition: Bank whose page this is.

dictionary.name: bank_category
dictionary.label: Bank category
dictionary.definition: Traditional incumbent or digital challenger. The axis BO-02 asks about.

dictionary.name: product_family
dictionary.label: Product family
dictionary.definition: Product family the page promotes. Comparisons are only valid within one family (DR-04).

dictionary.name: page_role
dictionary.label: Page role
dictionary.definition: What the page is for within the funnel.

dictionary.name: url
dictionary.label: Url
dictionary.definition: Full source URL as fetched.

dictionary.name: language
dictionary.label: Language
dictionary.definition: Language of the page version captured.

dictionary.name: captured_at
dictionary.label: Captured at
dictionary.definition: UTC timestamp of the fetch. Every conclusion is valid for this date only.

dictionary.name: collection_method
dictionary.label: Collection method
dictionary.definition: How the page was retrieved. Static fetch misses JavaScript-built layout (risk R-02). manual_capture is a page a person opened in a normal browser and saved, used where an edge/CDN declines automated traffic - the content is identical, but there is no HTTP status of our own and the capture time is the person's, not the pipeline's.

dictionary.name: robots_allowed
dictionary.label: Robots allowed
dictionary.definition: Whether robots.txt allowed this path for the user agent used, checked before fetching. Carried in the row so compliance evidence travels with the data (LC-01).

dictionary.name: snapshot_html_path
dictionary.label: Snapshot html path
dictionary.definition: Relative path to the stored raw HTML snapshot.

dictionary.name: screenshot_path
dictionary.label: Screenshot path
dictionary.definition: Relative path to the stored full-page screenshot.

dictionary.name: data_source
dictionary.label: Data source
dictionary.definition: Whether the row is a real capture or a synthetic fixture row. Guards against fixture data reaching a finding.

dictionary.name: extraction_model
dictionary.label: Extraction model
dictionary.definition: Provider and model that produced the model_assisted fields for this row, as "provider/model". Blank for rows with no model-assisted features.

dictionary.name: capture_quality
dictionary.label: Capture quality
dictionary.definition: Whether the captured page looks like a real campaign page. 'unusable' means an error/maintenance page or a shell that never rendered its content, and the row must be excluded from analysis.

dictionary.name: http_status
dictionary.label: Http status
dictionary.definition: HTTP status returned when the page was fetched. Anything other than 2xx is not a campaign page.

dictionary.name: shadow_hosts_flattened
dictionary.label: Shadow hosts flattened
dictionary.definition: Number of shadow roots inlined into the HTML before extraction. Above zero means the page is built from web components and would have been largely invisible to a light-DOM-only extractor.

dictionary.name: capture_quality_note
dictionary.label: Capture quality note
dictionary.definition: Why capture_quality got that verdict, in words, for the limitations section.

dictionary.name: word_count
dictionary.label: Words on the page
dictionary.definition: Visible words in the page body, excluding navigation, footer and cookie banner.

dictionary.name: sentence_count
dictionary.label: Sentences
dictionary.definition: Number of sentences in the page body.

dictionary.name: avg_sentence_length
dictionary.label: Words per sentence
dictionary.definition: Mean words per sentence.

dictionary.name: readability_score
dictionary.label: Readability
dictionary.definition: Readability index of the body text. Higher means easier.

dictionary.name: readability_formula
dictionary.label: Readability formula
dictionary.definition: Which readability formula produced readability_score.

dictionary.name: readability_band
dictionary.label: Readability band
dictionary.definition: Readability score bucketed into language-neutral bands, so it can cross languages.

dictionary.name: word_count_band
dictionary.label: Word count band
dictionary.definition: word_count bucketed into fixed-threshold bands, so it can be compared across languages.

dictionary.name: sentence_count_band
dictionary.label: Sentence count band
dictionary.definition: sentence_count bucketed into fixed-threshold bands, so it can be compared across languages.

dictionary.name: avg_sentence_length_band
dictionary.label: Avg sentence length band
dictionary.definition: avg_sentence_length bucketed into fixed-threshold bands, so it can be compared across languages.

dictionary.name: second_person_ratio_band

dictionary.name: first_person_plural_band

dictionary.name: disclaimer_word_share_band
dictionary.label: Disclaimer word share band

dictionary.name: text_to_image_ratio_band
dictionary.label: Text to image ratio band

dictionary.name: second_person_ratio

dictionary.name: first_person_plural_count

dictionary.definition: Occurrences of bank-as-we pronouns (wij/we, nous, we/our).

dictionary.name: question_count
dictionary.label: Questions asked
dictionary.definition: Number of question marks in body text.

dictionary.name: urgency_marker_count
dictionary.label: Urgency and deadline language
dictionary.definition: Occurrences of scarcity or deadline language, matched against a per-language term list (only until, limited offer, nog tot, offre limitee, ...).

dictionary.name: numeric_claim_count
dictionary.label: Figures and percentages quoted
dictionary.definition: Count of numeric claims in body text (percentages, amounts, durations).

dictionary.name: formality_score

dictionary.definition: How formal the register is. 1 = conversational, 5 = institutional.

dictionary.name: clarity_score

dictionary.definition: How easily a first-time reader grasps the offer. 1 = opaque, 5 = immediate.

dictionary.name: primary_product

dictionary.name: rate_shown

dictionary.name: rate_value_pct

dictionary.name: fab_level

dictionary.name: value_prop_clarity

dictionary.name: disclaimer_present

dictionary.name: animated_asset_count

dictionary.name: page_height_px
dictionary.label: Page length

dictionary.name: section_count

dictionary.name: text_image_layout
dictionary.label: Text and image arrangement
dictionary.definition: How the dominant pattern relates text and image: side by side (beside), one above the other (stacked), or text written directly on top of the image (overlaid, e.g. a full-bleed hero photo with a headline over it).

dictionary.name: mobile_first_design_signal
dictionary.label: Designed mobile-first
dictionary.definition: Whether the page's visual design reads as built mobile-first (single-column cards, large tap targets, minimal above-fold density) rather than desktop-first (multi-column, hover-dependent, dense), judged from the desktop screenshot. dictionary.definition: Does the page open with something that stops the reader?

dictionary.name: aida_interest

dictionary.definition: Does it give a reason to keep reading beyond the headline?

dictionary.name: aida_desire

dictionary.definition: Does it make the offer feel worth having, not just understood?

dictionary.name: aida_action

dictionary.name: aida_coverage_score

dictionary.label: Persuasion levers

dictionary.name: audience_segment
dictionary.label: Audience segment
dictionary.definition: Whether the page addresses an individual, a professional/self-employed activity, or both.

dictionary.name: is_bundled_offer
dictionary.label: Sells a bundle
dictionary.definition: Whether the page pushes a bundle (account + card + insurance + investment) in the same funnel, rather than one isolated product.

dictionary.name: cross_sell_delivery_model
dictionary.label: Cross sell delivery model
dictionary.definition: How a cross-sold product (insurance, investment) is delivered when one is offered - an in-house product with a dedicated advisor (bancassurance), a digital add-on distributed through a third-party partner with no advisor, or not applicable (nothing cross-sold on this page).

dictionary.name: target_personas
dictionary.label: Target personas
dictionary.definition: Which customer persona archetypes this page's copy/imagery explicitly addresses.

dictionary.name: cross_sold_products
dictionary.label: Cross sold products
dictionary.definition: Other product families this page cross-sells or cross-references alongside its own product_family.

dictionary.name: subscription_style_framing
dictionary.label: Subscription style framing
dictionary.definition: Whether the account tiers are framed as a subscription/plan (like a phone or streaming service) rather than a traditional banking "pack".

dictionary.name: rate_framing
dictionary.label: Rate framing
dictionary.definition: Whether the headline rate is the regulated base rate, a promotional bonus, a capped/tiered rate presented as the full rate, or no rate is shown.

dictionary.name: primary_cta_type
dictionary.label: Primary cta type
dictionary.definition: Whether the primary call to action is self-service online, booking an advisor/branch visit, or something else.

dictionary.name: switching_framing
dictionary.label: Switching framing
dictionary.definition: Whether the message reassures against switching away (retention) or actively encourages switching in (acquisition), if applicable at all.

dictionary.name: regulatory_disclosure_prominence
dictionary.label: Regulatory disclosure prominence
dictionary.definition: How visible the mandated disclosure THAT APPLIES TO THIS PAGE'S product_family is: APR/TAEG for mortgage, the deposit guarantee scheme for term_account/savings_account, a capital-at-risk warning for investment. not_applicable when no such disclosure is expected for this product_family (e.g. a plain current_account_pack with no credit component) - do not score it "absent" in that case, absent is reserved for a disclosure that IS expected but isn't shown.

dictionary.name: hidden_conditions_behind_free_claim
dictionary.label: “Free” with conditions attached
dictionary.definition: Whether "free" is the headline claim while conditions (minimum balance, usage requirement) sit in small print.

dictionary.name: esg_claim_specificity
dictionary.label: Esg claim specificity
dictionary.definition: Whether a sustainability claim carries a verifiable reference or figure, is an adjective only, or is absent.

dictionary.name: green_product_specific_benefit
dictionary.label: Names a concrete green benefit
dictionary.definition: Whether a concrete financial benefit (e.g. a rate discount) is explicitly tied to a green/energy-performance criterion, vs a generic sustainability claim.

dictionary.name: mentions_loyalty_or_referral
dictionary.label: Mentions loyalty or referral
dictionary.definition: Whether the page advertises a loyalty programme or a referral scheme ("invite a friend").

dictionary.name: images_have_alt_text
dictionary.label: Images carry alt text
dictionary.definition: Whether content images on the page carry non-empty alt text.

dictionary.name: meta_title
dictionary.label: Meta title
dictionary.definition: The <title> tag content - what the bank prioritises for organic search, often different from the page's visual message.

dictionary.name: institutional_trust_signal_present
dictionary.label: Invokes institutional trust
dictionary.definition: Whether the page invokes tenure, customer count, or ownership backing (e.g. state ownership) as a trust/safety argument.

dictionary.name: youth_student_targeting
dictionary.label: Targets students or young people
dictionary.definition: Whether a junior/student account or youth-oriented offer is promoted, as a long-horizon acquisition strategy.

dictionary.name: secondary_bank_positioning
dictionary.label: Positions as a second bank
dictionary.definition: Whether the bank frames itself as an addition to an existing bank ("keep your current bank, add us") rather than a full replacement.

dictionary.name: expat_cross_border_targeting
dictionary.label: Targets expats
dictionary.definition: Whether the page targets expats/international clients (e.g. English content framed around "moving to Belgium").

dictionary.name: branch_network_cited_as_benefit
dictionary.label: Cites its branch network
dictionary.definition: Whether the page explicitly cites physical branch/ATM network size as an advantage.

dictionary.name: fast_digital_onboarding_claim
dictionary.label: Promises fast digital sign-up
dictionary.definition: Whether the page claims a fast, frictionless digital account-opening process (e.g. "open an account in 5 minutes", no branch visit needed, instant approval).

dictionary.name: first_time_investor_targeting
dictionary.label: Targets first-time investors
dictionary.definition: Whether the page frames investing as a first step for a novice (e.g. "start with as little as", beginner glossary, low/no minimum) rather than assuming existing investment experience.

dictionary.name: senior_preretirement_targeting
dictionary.label: Targets pre-retirement
dictionary.definition: Whether the page targets a pre-retirement/senior life stage - pension planning, wealth transfer or succession, end-of-career estate management - as the entry point.

features.name: formality_score
features.label: Formality of tone
features.definition: How formal the register is. 1 = conversational, 5 = institutional.

rubric.1: Speaks like a friend. Contractions, slang, direct address throughout.
rubric.2: Informal but composed. Direct address, short sentences, no jargon.
rubric.4: Formal. Full forms of address, product and regulatory vocabulary.
rubric.5: Institutional and legalistic. Reads like a product sheet.

features.name: clarity_score
features.label: Clarity
features.definition: How easily a first-time reader grasps the offer. 1 = opaque, 5 = immediate.

rubric.1: Can't tell what's being offered without reading twice.
rubric.2: Vague - the product is named but the offer itself (rate, benefit, condition) is unclear.
rubric.3: Understandable with effort - the offer is there but buried among secondary information.
rubric.4: Clear - offer, audience and next step are identifiable at a glance.
rubric.5: Immediate - the value proposition is unmistakable within the first few seconds.

features.name: rate_prominence
features.label: How prominently the rate is shown
features.definition: Where the rate sits in the visual hierarchy.

rubric.hero: The rate is the largest or most visually dominant element on the page.
rubric.above_fold: The rate is visible without scrolling, but is not the dominant visual element.
rubric.below_fold: The rate only appears after scrolling.
rubric.absent: No rate is shown anywhere on the page.

features.name: value_prop_clarity
features.label: Clarity of the offer
features.definition: How clearly the page states what is offered, to whom, against which alternative.

rubric.1: No stated value proposition - reads like a product description, not an offer.
rubric.2: What is offered is named, but who it is for and the alternative are absent.
rubric.3: What and who are clear, but the implied alternative is absent or only implicit.
rubric.4: What, who and the implied alternative are all identifiable.
rubric.5: What, who and the alternative are explicit and quantified.

features.name: accent_locations
features.label: Where the brand colour appears
features.definition: Where the brand accent actually appears.

rubric.text: Accent colour used on headlines or body text.
rubric.icons: Accent colour used on icons or small graphic markers.
rubric.imagery: Accent colour appears within the photos, illustrations or renders themselves.
rubric.background: Accent colour used as a section or page background.
rubric.buttons: Accent colour used on call-to-action buttons or other interactive elements.

features.notes: Directly tests the deck's distinction - Fortis uses green "in text and icons, not in pictures", Belfius uses red "in text and pictures". sieg 15/09: this is a perceptual judgement call, independent from the automatic brand_colour_share (strict pixel-distance match on the hero image only). The two are expected to disagree sometimes - e.g. a human says "yes, accent in imagery" for a subtle tint that brand_colour_share's Euclidean tolerance doesn't count. Do not try to reconcile them; report both, a mismatch between "looks branded" and "measures as branded" is itself a finding.

features.name: text_image_layout
features.label: Text and image arrangement
features.definition: How the dominant pattern relates text and image: side by side (beside), one above the other (stacked), or text written directly on top of the image (overlaid, e.g. a full-bleed hero photo with a headline over it).

rubric.beside: Text and image sit side by side, both fully visible (e.g. photo left, text block right).
rubric.stacked: Image and text follow each other vertically, not overlapping.
rubric.overlaid: Text is written directly on top of the image (e.g. a full-bleed hero photo with a headline over it).

features.notes: The single observation the deck repeats for every bank. ING is called out as the one where "text and picture not anymore next to each other". sieg 15/09: no "no_image" value on purpose - a page with no image at all leaves this field null (nullable: true), it is not forced into one of the three categories above.

features.name: layout_archetype
features.label: Page layout pattern
features.definition: Overall structural pattern of the page.

rubric.hero_stacked: One large hero visual at the top, content stacked vertically below it.
rubric.split_columns: The page is organised into two or more side-by-side columns throughout.
rubric.card_grid: Content is organised as a grid of self-contained cards or tiles.
rubric.long_form: Continuous scrolling sections with no strong grid or card structure.

features.notes: sieg 15/09: real pages often mix patterns (e.g. a hero_stacked header over a card_grid body) - score the pattern of the FIRST SCREEN (above the fold), not the page as a whole, so raters have one consistent rule.

features.name: mobile_first_design_signal
features.label: Designed mobile-first
features.definition: Whether the page's visual design reads as built mobile-first (single-column cards, large tap targets, minimal above-fold density) rather than desktop-first (multi-column, hover-dependent, dense), judged from the desktop screenshot. Not a responsive/viewport measurement - this project only captures one fixed viewport.

rubric.True: Single-column, card-like blocks, large tap-friendly buttons, minimal density above the fold.
rubric.False: Multi-column layout, dense information, hover-dependent interactions.

features.name: aida_attention
features.label: Opens with something that stops the reader
features.definition: Does the page open with something that stops the reader?

rubric.True: Something on the first screen (headline, visual, number) is genuinely arresting, not generic.
rubric.False: The opening is generic enough that skipping it would lose nothing.

features.name: aida_interest
features.label: Gives a reason to keep reading
features.definition: Does it give a reason to keep reading beyond the headline?

rubric.True: There is a reason to keep reading beyond the headline - a specific detail, a question, a hinted benefit.
rubric.False: The page front-loads everything, or gives no reason to continue past the first line.

features.name: aida_desire
features.label: Makes the offer feel worth having
features.definition: Does it make the offer feel worth having, not just understood?

rubric.True: The offer is made to feel worth having - concrete benefit, social proof or emotional payoff, not only a spec sheet.
rubric.False: The page states facts (rate, features) without making the reader want the outcome.

features.name: aida_action
features.label: Has an unmistakable next step
features.definition: Is there an unmistakable next step?

rubric.True: There is one unmistakable next step - a single call to action, or several CTAs clearly segmented by audience/situation so each visitor still has exactly one obvious path (e.g. "not retired yet" vs "already retired").
rubric.False: No clear call to action, or several CTAs competing for the same visitor with no clear way to tell which applies.

features.name: persuasion_levers
features.label: Persuasion levers
features.definition: Which of Cialdini's six persuasion principles are used on the page.

rubric.reciprocity: The page offers something free or upfront before asking for commitment.
rubric.commitment: The page asks for a small first step that implies a larger one.
rubric.social_proof: The page cites other customers, ratings, review counts, or user numbers.
rubric.authority: The page invokes expertise, credentials, regulator backing, or institutional tenure.
rubric.liking: The page uses a friendly tone, relatable imagery, or a likeable brand voice to build affinity.
rubric.scarcity: The page uses deadlines, limited availability, or "only until" language.

features.notes: Turns the vague word "persuasive" into a closed, countable list.
